title: Read and validate server searchParams
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/search/page.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Request no q, q=books and repeated q values.
Build with the promised route-prop type.
Verify hostile text renders as text rather than executable HTML.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: A query parameter can be missing or repeated, and reading it can require request-time rendering.
Request no q, q=books and repeated q values.
alternativeApproaches: Separate request-dependent results from the static shell and use a deliberate Suspense boundary when using Cache Components. Cache public results only with keys that include all admitted search/filter dimensions.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Request no q, q=books and repeated q values.
Build with the promised route-prop type.
Verify hostile text renders as text rather than executable HTML.
nextjsPractice.next15: Await promised page searchParams even while temporary synchronous access exists.
nextjsPractice.next16: Await is required. Plain-object server searchParams is distinct from the client useSearchParams interface.
